description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 against ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite (MAT=30), found while quantifying temperature-grid thinning. Regression-locked by
tests/thermal_temperature_thinning.rs::production_interpolation_leaves_the_bracket_above_half_an_ev. NOT FIXED --
it needs its own change and its own V&V.

THE DEFECT. sigma_inel(E,T) is monotone in T across the tabulated grid, so an interpolated value at a temperature
between two tabulated ones MUST lie between their two cross sections. The production interpolation does not:

  at 393.15 K, E = 3.9 eV:  interpolated 4.4175 b   against the bracket [4.6097, 4.6367]
                            -- roughly 4-5% BELOW the lower bracketing value, i.e. outside it entirely

Same behaviour at 523.15 K, 900 K and 1400 K. About 1% low at 0.5 eV. CORRECT at and below 0.1 eV.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BEEN CAUGHT. The existing coverage (tests/thermal_graphite_coherent.rs) checks 0.0253 eV only,
which is inside the region where the interpolation behaves. The defect lives above ~0.5 eV.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERY non-tabulated temperature request today. The graphite evaluation tabulates 296, 400, 500, 600,
700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1600, 2000 K; the IAEA HTR-10 B1-B4 benchmarks are at 293.15 / 393.15 / 523.15 K, all of which
are interpolated. So this is on the HTR-10 critical path, not a corner case.

SEVERITY IN CONTEXT: at 0.0253 eV, where the thermal spectrum lives, the interpolation is fine, and coherent elastic
(~90% of the thermal cross section) is unaffected. The error is in the epithermal tail of the inelastic channel. It
is a real defect and a bounded one -- do not report it as breaking the thermal spectrum without measuring that.

NOT THE CAUSE, already ruled out by the reporting agent: zero-endpoint handling. A PreserveZeros variant gave
bit-identical statistics, and the reconstruction was verified monotone. What was NOT established is why ln S is so
non-linear in T in the far tail -- only that it is. Start there.

RELATED: op-cjw.22 (inelastic temperature interpolation) is filed P4 on the stated assumption that target temps are
tabulated exactly. That assumption fails for HTR-10, and this bead is direct evidence the interpolation it defers is
actually wrong rather than merely absent. Consider re-prioritising or merging.

Also fixed in passing while measuring this, and worth knowing: IncoherentInelastic was DISCARDING the inelastic LI
temperature-interpolation codes -- the same class of defect as op-1y4y on the elastic side. mf7.rs now retains them
(IncoherentInelastic::temp_interp), so the tape's own LI=4 is read rather than assumed.
title: njoy THERMR DEFECT: inelastic temperature interpolation leaves its tabulated bracket above ~0.5 eV (4-5% low at 3.9 eV)
